target.title: fix(bridge): never return empty Data for error responses
target.body:
## Summary

Bridge failures could return empty bytes when encoding an error response failed. Clients then saw EOF or a secondary decode failure instead of a bridge error.

## Change

- Route server decode/handler failures and rejected host peers through one error-response encoder.
- Return the caller encoder's non-empty payload when available.
- Fall back to fixed, compile-time JSON that always decodes as an `internalError` when encoding throws or returns empty bytes.
- Avoid interpolating dynamic strings into last-resort JSON, so arbitrary control characters cannot corrupt the wire response.
- Cover malformed requests, thrown encoding, empty encoder output, control characters, and a real unauthorized Unix-socket peer.

## Why

The old `try? ... ?? Data()` paths converted an error-reporting failure into a zero-byte response. This is the same reliability class as #209: successful or error-bearing operations must return the artifact or structured state they promise, never an unreadable placeholder.

## Proof

Exact candidate: `cb6681e48ee2efac65bfb402906ca0f5bb8ae839`

- `swift test --package-path Core/PeekabooCore --filter PeekabooBridgeEncodeErrorTests` — 4 tests / 1 suite passed.
- `swift test --package-path Apps/CLI --filter PeekabooBridgeHostUnauthorizedResponseTests` — 1 real Unix-socket integration test / 1 suite passed.
- `pnpm run test:safe` — 628 tests / 71 suites passed.
- Live candidate CLI: version reported `cb6681e4`; all three macOS permission checks granted; 165 running apps enumerated successfully.
- Source-blind behavior contract: malformed requests and unauthorized peers both produced non-empty decodable errors; no EOF.
- Full-branch autoreview against `origin/main`: clean, no accepted/actionable findings.
- Exact-head CI: https://github.com/openclaw/Peekaboo/actions/runs/28682134869

## Origin

The empty fallback was introduced in `27eceede8` and had remained in the bridge server and host error paths.

Related: #209, #210.
